item.title: Police urged to investigate London event advertising settlement-linked Israeli agency
item.description:
Police urged to investigate London event advertising settlement-linked Israeli agency

Submitted by Imran Mulla on Wed, 11/04/2026 - 11:23
Activists protested at the World Travel Market event, which began on Tuesday and is advertising the Jerusalem Development Authority
A line of police wait to move in as protesters gather around the corner in support of the Palestine Action activist group outside the Supreme Court in central London on 4 November 2026 (AFP)
Off

The Metropolitan Police have been urged to investigate the participation of an Israeli agency involved in the construction of illegal settlements at an international travel event in London.

MEE revealed last week that the World Travel Market (WTM) event this week, which faced a pro-Palestine protest on Tuesday and will continue until Thursday, was set to feature a stand run by the Israeli government's tourist office.

The International Centre of Justice for Palestinians (ICJP, a UK-based legal group, sent a letter to the Met Police's war crimes team on Tuesday demanding the "urgent investigation and consideration of preventative measures in relation to the reported participation of the Jerusalem Development Authority (JDA), through its tourism platform iTravelJerusalem, at World Travel Market (WTM) London".

Activists with the Palestine Solidarity Campaign (PSC) protested next to Israel's stand on Tuesday, holding a banner reading "Every settlement is a war crime".

Video footage showed two activists being physically removed from the event by security guards.

Ryvka Barnard, the deputy director of the PSC, told MEE: "The Israeli state's presence at the World Travel Market in London is an utter disgrace. 

"In September, when the foreign secretary acknowledged that Israel's occupation is illegal, he said he would ban the advertising of illegal settlements. But that's exactly what's happening here. 

"This is now a test for the Labour government. Will it stick to its word, intervene to shut down this stall and call for criminal investigations into its organisers, or will it reveal that those were just empty words?"

Will it stick to its word, intervene to shut down this stall and call for criminal investigations into its organisers, or will it reveal that those were just empty words?"

The Israeli stand is shared by numerous Israeli companies and organisations, including "iTravelJerusalem", which promotes tourism in Israeli-occupied East Jerusalem and is managed by the Jerusalem Development Authority (JDA).

The JDA, a statutory agency of the Israeli government and the Jerusalem municipality, carries out development initiatives across Jerusalem and has been heavily involved in the construction and expansion of illegal Israeli settlements on occupied Palestinian territory.

Since 2023 the JDA has a contract with Finn Partners, a global marketing agency, to advertise Jerusalem as a tourism destination in Britain.

'These circumstances warrant urgent investigation'

The ICJP's letter to the Met Police, seen by MEE, says: "Of particular concern is the commercial relationship between the JDA and WTM London... including the possibility that the organisers may receive exhibition fees or derive other financial benefits from the participation of an agency reportedly implicated in settlement related activities.

"We consider that these circumstances warrant urgent investigation into potential offences."

MEE has asked the Met Police and WTM for comment.

Exclusive: London event advertises Israeli agency building illegal settlements
Read More »

This comes after 15 MPs wrote to the British government on Monday calling for "urgent action" on the event.

The MPs demanded that the government "contact the organisers of WTM London and require the removal of exhibitors and promotional material where their participation would facilitate or promote illegal Israeli settlements".

Last month, the British government recognised Israel's occupation of Palestinian territory as illegal and announced comprehensive sanctions on Israeli settlements.

According to a 2025 report by the Office of the European Union Representative for the West Bank and Gaza Strip, the JDA planned "for the eviction of the Umm Haroun compound - home to approximately 40 Palestinian families - and the construction of a 320-unit settlement" in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood. 

In 2020, a JDA project to build a cable car in Jerusalem, which would involve the uprooting of trees and displacement of infrastructure including water, sewage and telecommunications, was approved by the Israeli government.

The JDA also plans to build a large settlement housing project next to the Palestinian community of Beit Safafa in East Jerusalem.

Hussam Zomlot, the Palestinian ambassador to Britain, said in response to MEE's report last Thursday: "Next week Israeli companies guilty of ethnic cleansing will be platformed at [WTM London]."

Zomlot added: "The UK government must now turn their words into action: enforce these commitments and ensure those complicit in illegal occupation and settlements face real consequences."

item.title: Israel faces constitutional crisis as Netanyahu challenges election result
'I think a part of it was Iran': Trump acknowledges war's impact on midterm election losses
item.description:
'I think a part of it was Iran': Trump acknowledges war's impact on midterm election losses

Submitted by MEE staff on Wed, 11/04/2026 - 10:21
The prices of goods and petrol have risen in the US as a direct result of the unpopular war in Iran, and played a role in the Democrats gaining control of the Senate and House of Representatives
US President Donald Trump speaks during a round table at the White House in Washington, DC, US, 21 October 2026 (Kevin Lamarque/ Reuters)
Off

US President Donald Trump acknowledged on Wednesday that the war on Iran played a part in the Republican party’s sweeping midterm election losses. 

Democrats won control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, with politicians who had campaigned on their opposition to the war scoring notable victories.

In separate interviews reflecting on the reasons behind his party’s heavy defeats, Trump said: “I think a part of it was Iran… Iran was a piece of it.”

Nevertheless, the US president stood by his decision to join Israel in attacking Iran, which also went against the “no new wars” messaging of his 2024 presidential campaign.

“I did the right thing,” Trump told the Wall Street Journal. “I would have done it again.”

The US and Israel went to war with Iran at the end of February, after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had reportedly presented Trump with intelligence from Mossad convincing him that doing so would lead the Iranian people to rise up and overthrow their government. 

Cost of living

But despite killing a slew of Iranian leaders, including former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, the government in Tehran has remained intact and the Iranian military has seized control of the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices skyrocketing across the globe.  

The attendant rise in the cost of petrol and other goods at home in the US was a theme of the Democrats’ messaging, with candidates across the country blaming the war for the high cost of living.

Speaking to Middle East Eye’s Rhana Natour, Abbas Alawieh, founder of the Uncommitted Movement and candidate for the Michigan State Senate, says voters lost trust in Democratic leadership in 2024 because they were out of touch with ordinary working people in America. https://t.co/U2Jf5dukKs

— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) November 4, 2026

Trump has chopped and changed his stated priorities for the war, which has remained consistently unpopular with Americans. 

Asked after the midterm results about reports that he was considering using a nuclear weapon on Iran, Trump said: “I don’t need it, we’ve knocked them out already, 90 percent.”

In Tehran, the US election results were met with satisfaction. “Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message,” Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Wednesday on X.

item.title: Iran’s Khamenei says US election results will not end hostility towards Tehran
item.description:
Iran’s Khamenei says US election results will not end hostility towards Tehran

Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei says Washington will continue its confrontation with Tehran despite the Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories.

In a message carried by state news agency IRNA, he rejected suggestions that “factional shifts” would “dissuade it from its hostility towards the Iranian nation”.

He said Washington seeks the “unconditional surrender of the Iranian nation”.

Referring to the US-Israeli war on Iran, Khamenei said the US had “suffered an irreversible decline” after a “self-made scandal”, adding that “the process of its collapse has accelerated”.

item.title: Gaza volunteer surgeon Adam Hamawy wins US House seat in New Jersey
item.description:
Gaza volunteer surgeon Adam Hamawy wins US House seat in New Jersey

Democrat Adam Hamawy, who treated Palestinians in Gaza during Israel’s genocide, has defeated Republican Gregg Mele to represent New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District.

The 57-year-old former US Army combat surgeon campaigned against military assistance to Israel and other countries committing human rights violations.

He has also condemned the war on Iran as “illegal and immoral”. In a May interview he accused Washington of “catering to special interests of the defense contractors and war mongers and with organizations like [American Israel Public Affairs Committee] AIPAC and Israel’s special interests.”

Hamawy joined missions to Gaza in 2024 and 2025 through the Palestinian American Medical Association, with coordination from the World Health Organization.
